title: Console prio canvas: rapid grooming (Aug 2026)
content:
Context:
This is the working output from a 90-minute rapid grooming session to produce a small cut for the next two-week sprint focused on Console UX features for rollout/route visibility and lightweight model controls. Goal: pick a coherent subset that unlocks customer-facing observability and the model variant selector wireframe so Solutions can demo Dedicated->Private fallbacks in upcoming POC calls.

Session notes (high level):
- Timebox: 90 minutes on 2026-08-03. Attendees: Maya, Jonah, Priya, Luca, SRE standby (Sam).
- Outcome: prioritized 6 candidate stories; 3 targeted for Sprint N (must), 2 for Sprint N+1 (should), 1 for backlog watch (could).
- Tone: pragmatic, demoable MVPs. Prefer smaller UX increments + feature flags rather than big UI rewrites.

Prioritization canvas (visual mental model used):
- X axis: User value (low -> high)
- Y axis: Implementation risk / infra coordination (low -> high)
- Horizontal cut: demoable within 2 weeks (left) vs requires infra work (right)
We placed items to maximize demoable high-value with low infra risk into the "Must" bucket.

Must (target Sprint N - demo + ship):
1) CON-742 Model Variant Selector (M) — owner: Jonah Kim — estimate: M
   - Summary: compact selector in route config to pick primary/secondary model variants and enable automatic fallback.
   - Wireframe notes: inline dropdown that shows variant name, token cost multiplier, and latency estimate (pop-over). Quick toggle to enable "auto-fallback to region/model-tier".
   - Acceptance criteria: selector persists to route config; on change, console calls config API and shows success toast; pop-over shows mocked latency/cost numbers; feature gated behind FF:console-model-variant.
   - Dependencies: backend config API (CON-600, infra small change), feature flag infra (exists).
   - Linked demo flow: create route -> choose model variant -> simulate model unavailable -> observe fallback toast.

2) CON-801 Route Health + Fallback Indicator (S) — owner: Priya Desai — estimate: M
   - Summary: add a thin optimistic status row in route list showing health (green/yellow/red) + small fallback icon when automatic fallback is enabled. Hover shows recent fallback count (last 24h).
   - Wireframe notes: keep list density high; icon only (no heavy graph). Hover card includes links to the route timeline and a link to logs.
   - Acceptance criteria: status icon reflects synthetic probe (SRE probe), hover card shows count (0-99), clicking timeline opens the route timeline page.
   - Dependencies: synthetic probe metric (SRE, ticket SRE-122), minor telemetry schema update.

3) CON-823 Batching Inspector (S) — owner: Luca Moretti — estimate: M
   - Summary: quick visual for batching configuration per model/route: current batch size target, observed average latency, suggested tweak (from Optimize heuristics) with one-click apply.
   - Wireframe notes: small inspector panel on the route details page; suggested tweak is a single CTA (apply suggestion).
   - Acceptance criteria: shows current batch target, shows observed average measured over last 1h, button opens confirm modal; accepts when backend apply endpoint returns 200.
   - Dependencies: metrics endpoint for batching (ENG: METRICS-44).

Should (Sprint N+1):
4) CON-759 Rollout Mini-Timeline (should) — owner: Maya Patel — estimate: L
   - Summary: micro timeline in route page that summarizes active rollout (canary % over time, last rollback). Useful for quick QA.
   - Wireframe notes: horizontal sparkline with hover annotations; lightweight, read-only.
   - Dependencies: rollout timeline backend (RO-12), likely more infra coordination.

5) CON-660 Cost-per-token badge (should) — owner: Jonah Kim — estimate: S
   - Summary: show estimated cost-per-token per model in selector popover (derived from pricing table + quantization profile).
   - Wireframe notes: small gray text line under model name: "$0.0008 / token est". Link to cost explainer.
   - Dependencies: pricing table service (billing team).

Could / Watchlist:
6) CON-905 Private Badge + Quick-start (could) — owner: Priya Desai — estimate: S
   - Summary: cosmetic but high impact for sales: show a "Private" badge in routes deployed to private control plane + a one-click link to private deployment quickstart.
   - Notes: deprioritize until remaining items are shipped.

Wireframe annotations (quick sketches captured in notes):
- Model Variant Selector: dropdown row layout: left: name (mono), middle: two badges (latency, cost), right: three-dot menu for advanced -> opens panel with KV cache settings. When hover on cost badge, show tooltip with pricing breakdown + link to Cost-per-token doc.
- Route Health indicator: use 12px icon, color blind palettes, accessible tooltip text. In mobile view, show indicator on route card leading edge.
- Batching Inspector: sample schema for the inspector: [batch_target: int, observed_qps: float, avg_latency_ms: int, suggestion: {new_batch:int, rationale}] — UI should gracefully handle missing metrics by showing "insufficient data" and CTAs to run a synthetic load.

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: backend rollout timeline and probe metrics may not be available in time. Mitigation: build UI to show placeholders + link to feature flag toggle; have demo mode with mocked metrics for POC.
- Risk: cost data requires billing team coordination. Mitigation: show estimated cost from local pricing table (read-only) and label as "estimate".

Open questions (need answers before sprint planning):
- What SLA do we show for the route health indicator? (ops input) -> action: Sam to confirm by 2026-08-06.
- Billing: can we expose unit price per quantized model variant? -> action: ping billing (Aisha) for schema and scope.
- UX: is a two-line row for model selector acceptable for dense route lists? -> action: UX critique scheduled 2026-08-05.

Acceptance test plan (brief):
- CON-742: E2E test flows: save selector -> API receives correct payload -> simulate model down -> confirm fallback shows in timeline and fallback count increments.
- CON-801: unit test for hover card rendering, integration test for probe-based color change.
- CON-823: integration test around batching suggestion apply and rollback via API.

Metrics for success (first 30 days after ship):
- Adoption: % of routes with model variant explicitly set within 30 days (target >= 25%).
- Observability: reduction in dev support calls that ask "which model served this request" (qualitative CS feedback).
- Automation: % of suggested batching changes applied via inspector (target 10%).

Next steps / immediate todo list:
- [ ] Sync with SRE on probe availability (Sam) — due 2026-08-06
- [ ] Confirm pricing schema with Billing (Aisha) — due 2026-08-07
- [ ] Create 3 small PRs: wireframe-only HTML/CSS (no backend) for CON-742/CON-801/CON-823 to unblock design reviews — owner: Luca — target 2026-08-09
- [ ] Add feature flags for model-variant and batching-inspector in FF service — owner: Eng infra — ticket FF-19
- [ ] Draft demo script for sales POC (show model selector + fallback) — owner: Maya — draft due 2026-08-10

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep density high; customers on Dedicated/Dedicated trial like compact UIs they can scan.
- If backend takes longer, swap CON-660 in for CON-823 — lower infra friction.
- Remember to capture screenshots of the demo mode for the sales playbook.

Meeting artifacts: saved quick wireframes in the PR and a short Loom demo mock (see linked_artifacts).

If you want to re-run the prio canvas remotely: open this doc, move cards from "should" to "must" and re-evaluate dependencies.

End of doc.
